title: About page's GitHub and Documentation links are placeholders that 404 / do not resolve
what_happened: Settings > About offers three link buttons: GitHub, Documentation, Discord. GitHub opens https://github.com/skotiq-astro, which returns HTTP 404 -- the real project repo is https://github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq (HTTP 200, per the repo README badge). Documentation opens https://skotiq.astro/docs; 'skotiq.astro' does not resolve in DNS at all (.astro is not a delegated TLD). Discord opens https://discord.gg/skotiq, which is not a Skotiq invite. Clicking GitHub in the app produced no error banner -- the launch is reported as successful and the user is dropped on a 404.
expected: The three community links a shipped app puts on its About page must point at the real destinations: github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq, the docs (docs/index.md is what the README points at), and a real Discord invite -- or the button should not exist.
repro: gear icon > Settings > About > click GitHub. Then: curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://github.com/skotiq-astro -> 404; getent hosts skotiq.astro -> no answer.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-15.png (the three buttons rendered). curl: github.com/skotiq-astro -> 404, github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq -> 200, skotiq.astro -> DNS FAILS.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/about_settings.dart:102,109,116 (and the mobile duplicates at :102/:109/:116 vs desktop :128/:135/:142)
proposed_fix: Hoist the three URLs into one const block and set them to the real repo/docs/invite; add a launch-failure path that surfaces the URL (the existing showErrorSnackBar only fires when canLaunchUrl is false, which is not the failure mode here).
verdict_reasoning: Verified at source and over the network. about_settings.dart hard-codes the three URLs twice (mobile Wrap :102/:109/:116, desktop Row :128/:135/:142), exactly as cited. curl https://github.com/skotiq-astro -> 404; curl https://github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq -> 200; getent hosts skotiq.astro -> no answer (.astro is not a delegated TLD, so Documentation can never resolve). The Discord claim is true but for a sharper reason than stated: discord.gg/skotiq 301s to discord.com/invite/skotiq and the Discord API returns a VALID invite to guild 1370106030754631690 'Skotiq Gaming Community' -- an unrelated gaming server, so the button works and drops the user in a stranger's Discord, which is worse than a dead link. _launchUrl only surfaces an error when canLaunchUrl/launchUrl returns false, which a 404 page never does, so 'no error banner' is correct by construction.

title: Paired devices live in ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db -- outside the app database, outside the configured data dir, and split across two stores
what_happened: I launched a completely fresh scratch profile (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-system/data, --fresh, empty skotiq.db). Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing immediately listed 12 devices paired 6/15/2026 and 7/20/2026 -- the developer's real, months-old pairings. They are not in skotiq.db; PairingDatabase opens getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/pairing.db, i.e. ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db, which ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR entirely. Two such stores exist on this machine: ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db (12 active rows, mtime Aug 1) and ~/Skotiq/pairing.db (0 rows, mtime Jul 29) -- the same install has written to two different locations depending on how getApplicationDocumentsDirectory resolved.
expected: Long-lived remote credentials belong in the app database (or at minimum under the configured data dir) so that (a) Backup & Restore captures them, (b) moving the data directory moves them, (c) they cannot silently fork into two stores. As shipped, restoring a backup on a new machine silently loses every pairing, and a launch context where XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR differs presents an empty device list with no error.
repro: drive_linux.py start --profile <new> --fresh (scratch data dir) > Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing. Observe 12 devices. sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/<profile>/data/skotiq.db '.tables' -> no pairing tables. sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db 'select count(*) from paired_devices where is_active=1' -> 12, matching the UI exactly. ls ~/Skotiq/pairing.db -> a second, empty store.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-22.png (12 devices in a fresh profile). UI count 12 == DB is_active count 12. Device names/dates match row-for-row (Dashboard 2026-06-15, Android companion 2026-07-20 x3...).
proposed_fix: Resolve the pairing DB through the same directory resolver the main database uses (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR-aware application-support dir), and migrate any existing Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db on first run. Include it in the backup manifest.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced from a --fresh scratch profile (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/v-settings-system/data). Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing immediately listed 13 devices paired 6/15/2026, 7/20 x3, 7/22, 7/25 x3, 7/26 -- months older than the profile. The scratch skotiq.db has NO pairing table; sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db 'select count(*) ... is_active=1' returns 13, matching the UI count exactly and the names row-for-row. (Finding said 12; it is 13 now because concurrent audit agents paired since -- the count tracking the shared store IS the defect.) Cited location is exact: pairing_database.dart:401-410 _openConnection uses getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/pairing.db with no data-dir override anywhere. Two-store claim holds: ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db (13 active, mtime Aug 1) and ~/Skotiq/pairing.db (0 rows, mtime Jul 29).

title: Backups are written to ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups regardless of the configured data directory, so bundles from different databases pile into one undifferentiated 'Recent Backups' list
what_happened: I launched a brand-new scratch profile with SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-system/data and an empty skotiq.db. Settings > Backup & Restore immediately listed 8 'Recent Backups' dated Aug 1 -- the developer's real bundles -- and reported 'Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 10:27'. The backup directory is ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups and ignores the data-dir override entirely, so this sandboxed instance also *wrote* into it: skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-27-37, -27-44, -27-45 and -30-25 are snapshots of my throwaway database (the 10:30 one records profilesCount: 0, taken right after I deleted every profile) sitting in the same list as the real ones. Nothing in the row -- name, size, date, icon -- says which database a bundle came from. A user with two installs, or anyone who has ever moved their data directory, is one click away from restoring a foreign configuration over their live one. As with pairing.db there are also two directories on this machine (~/Documents/Skotiq/backups with 9 bundles and ~/Skotiq/backups with 4), i.e. the same install has written backups to two places.
expected: Backups belong under the configured data directory, and each row should show what it contains (profiles/sequences/targets counts are already in the bundle metadata) and which install/machine wrote it. The bundle already carries appVersion and platform; add a database/install id and show it.
repro: drive_linux.py start --profile <new> --fresh > Settings > Backup & Restore. The list is non-empty on a first-ever launch. ls ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups -> the same 8 files, plus new skotiq_autosave_* written by the sandbox. python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('.../skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-30-25.892145.nsbackup'))['metadata'])" -> profilesCount 0, i.e. my scratch DB.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-59.png (Recent Backups list mixing Aug 1 and Aug 2 bundles). Directory listing of ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups and ~/Skotiq/backups. Bundle metadata quoted above.
where: the backup service's directory resolution (getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups) rather than the SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR-aware resolver used by skotiq.db
proposed_fix: Resolve the backup directory through the same data-dir resolver as the main database; stamp an install id into the bundle and show bundle contents (profiles/sequences/targets) in each Recent Backups row.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on a first-ever launch. Settings > Backup & Restore came up with a NON-EMPTY list -- 9 bundles dated Aug 1/Aug 2 this profile never created -- and 'Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 12:03'. Merely opening the screen also WROTE into the shared dir: ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups gained autosaves at 12-03-46/47/48 whose metadata is my throwaway DB (settingsCount 121, profilesCount 0), listed alongside the developer's real bundles. A fourth file appeared at 12-03-53 with profilesCount 1 while my DB had zero profiles -- a CONCURRENT audit instance writing into the same list, i.e. the finding's two-installs scenario happening live. `find /tmp/ns-audit/v-settings-system -iname '*backup*'` returns nothing. Root cause pinned: backup_service.dart:1025-1030 _getBackupDirectory -> getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups; the _backupDirectoryProvider override (:121/:149) is referenced from exactly one place in the repo, backup_service_listing_test.dart:34, so production has no data-dir-aware path. Rows render name + size + date only, so nothing identifies the source database.

title: Restore silently drops a backed-up equipment profile when its row id is already taken, and still reports 'Restored 123 items'
what_happened: The bundle skotiq_backup_2026-08-02T10-43-32.295333.nsbackup contains exactly one equipment profile: {"id": 3, "name": "Backup Test Rig"} (metadata: settingsCount 122, profilesCount 1 -> 123 items). Locally, row id 3 existed but had been renamed to 'Local Work Do Not Lose'. I restored that bundle. The toast said 'Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' The DB afterwards: 3|Local Work Do Not Lose|1 -- one profile, the local one, unchanged. 'Backup Test Rig' was neither inserted nor applied over row 3; it was dropped on the floor. The same restore into a database where id 3 was free DID bring the profile back (I verified that first, after deleting every row), so the discriminator is the id collision, not the bundle. The count in the message is the bundle's item count, not the number of items actually applied, so it is a claim the app has not checked.
expected: Restore must not key library items on the backup's row ids -- ids are local and get reused as soon as you delete the highest row. Re-key on content (name) or insert with a fresh id, and report what was actually written ('122 settings updated, 1 profile added, 0 skipped'), never the bundle's own count.
repro: Create a profile, Create Backup, rename that profile (or delete it and create another that takes the same rowid), then restore the bundle from Recent Backups. Toast claims all items restored; sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' shows the backed-up profile is absent.
evidence: Bundle JSON equipmentProfiles[0] = id 3 / 'Backup Test Rig'; DB after restore = 3|Local Work Do Not Lose|1; tree after restore = 'panel: Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' Control case: with equipment_profiles emptied, the same bundle restored the profile back as id 3.
where: the restore path in the backup service (row-id-keyed upsert/ignore for equipmentProfiles) called from packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/backup_screen.dart
location_wrong: cited only as 'the restore path in the backup service ... called from backup_screen.dart'; the defect lines are sequence_codec.dart:50-52 (id taken from the bundle), :114 (InsertMode.insertOrIgnore) and :116 (unconditional count++), with backup_screen.dart:267 forcing replaceExisting:false and :275 printing the count
proposed_fix: Strip ids on restore and insert as new rows (matching existing rows by name to update), and build the success message from the write result rather than from bundle metadata.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own bundle plus a control case. Bundle skotiq_backup_2026-08-02T12-13-00 contained equipmentProfiles[0] = {id:1,'VSS Renamed B'}, metadata settingsCount 122 + profilesCount 1 = 123. I renamed local row id 1 to 'VSS Local Keep' and restored: toast read verbatim 'Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' while sqlite3 afterwards showed 1|VSS Local Keep -- the backed-up profile neither inserted nor applied. CONTROL: with equipment_profiles emptied, the SAME bundle restored it back as 1|VSS Renamed B, so the id collision is the discriminator. Mechanism confirmed in code: _importProfiles inserts with the backup's row id under InsertMode.insertOrIgnore and increments count unconditionally, so itemsRestored is rows ATTEMPTED, not rows written. One nuance in the app's favour that the finding omits: the confirm dialog hedges with 'library items from the backup may be added' -- but the toast then states a definite count it never checked. P1 retained.
